title: 1-Year Outcomes of Endovascular Repair of Zone 0/1 Aortic Arch Lesions with a Thoracic Branched Endoprosthesis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The GORE® TAG® Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis (TBE) pivotal non-randomized, multicenter, prospective trial evaluated 1-year outcomes in patients at high risk for open surgical repair undergoing aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta endovascular repair (Zone 0/1). METHODS: Endpoints evaluated from endovascular procedure through 12 months included aortic-related death, disabling stroke, permanent paraplegia or paraparesis, new onset renal failure, and unanticipated reintervention. Core-lab identified endpoints included aortic rupture or enlargement (≥5 mm), Type I/III endoleak, device integrity, device migration, fistula, patency, and new dissection. RESULTS: The 77 enrolled patients had aneurysm (n=50), dissection (n=24), or other isolated lesion types (n=3); 90.9% had a Zone 0 proximal stent landing zone. Patients were a mean age of 70.8±10.8 years, 66.2% male, and 57.1% white and all had the aortic and side branch component implanted. Technical success was 94.8%. Early outcomes to 12 months included 8 (10.4%) aortic-related deaths, 6 (7.8%) disabling strokes (all aneurysm cohort), 4 (5.2%) unanticipated reintervention, 2 (2.6%) aortic ruptures, and 1 (1.3%) renal failure. Type IA/IB or Type III endoleaks occurred in 6 (7.8%) patients. Loss of side branch patency occurred in 1 (1.3%) patient. There was no permanent paraplegia or paraparesis or loss of device integrity or migration. A total of five patients had aortic enlargement; none required reintervention. CONCLUSIONS: Early data from this prospective investigation of the TBE device in Zone 0/1 applications signals that the device is a reasonable therapeutic alternative in patients with appropriate anatomy deemed high risk for open arch surgery.

title: Automated Detection of Endoleaks in CT Angiography Using a Single Deep Learning Model.
abstract: AIM: Detecting endoleaks on post-EVAR CT scans, especially in the presence of artifacts caused by embolic agents like Onyx, is a challenging but critical task. In this study, we propose a deep learning-based method for endoleak detection using a single object detection model. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective dataset comprising 249 CT scans was used, divided into training (129 scans) and test (120 scans) datasets. Ground truth annotations were obtained through 3D manual segmentation, and a preprocessing pipeline was applied. The model was trained on slices extracted from the training dataset and validated using standard metrics, including sensitivity, specificity, and AUC. RESULTS: The model achieved high performance at both the per-slice and per-series levels. Per-slice detection yielded a ROC AUC of 96%, with a sensitivity of 91%, specificity of 93%, PPV of 55%, and NPV of 99%. At the per-series level, sensitivity and specificity were 93% and 95%, respectively. Notably, our method introduces a per-slice detection metric, which was not reported in previous studies, and uses a single model, making it computationally efficient and easy to train. CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates the feasibility of using deep learning for endoleak detection, offering a robust and efficient tool for clinical practice. Future work could focus on expanding the dataset and integrating additional predictive capabilities, such as endoleak classification and localization.

title: In Vitro Development and Evaluation of an Endovascular Islet Cell Stent for Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.
abstract: PURPOSE: To describe the in vitro development and benchtop evaluation of the IsletStent, an endovascular biologic stent-graft incorporating expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) semipermeable membranes, designed for portal venous delivery of pancreatic islets as a treatment for type 1 diabetes mellitus. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Prototypes with a 0.22 μm pore ePTFE membrane were seeded with murine (approximately 5,000-6,000 islet equivalents [IEQ]) or human (approximately 10,000 IEQ) islets. A benchtop normothermic perfusion circuit simulated intravascular deployment. Glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) was assessed in a repeated-measures design (n = 4 devices per experiment); murine islet-seeded devices were perfused under zero (0 mM), low (2.8 mM), and high (28 mM) glucose, and human islet-seeded devices under low and high glucose only, with insulin quantified by ELISA. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling under idealized, non-physiologic single-fluid conditions evaluated candidate device geometries. RESULTS: Murine islet-seeded devices demonstrated glucose-responsive insulin secretion: 3-hour insulin concentrations were 83 ± 8 vs. 145 ± 20 μIU/mL under low vs. high glucose (p = 0.02), and secretion rates were 5,344 ± 144 vs. 6,795 ± 503 μIU/hr (p = 0.008). Human islet-seeded devices responded concordantly, with 3-hour insulin concentrations of 229 ± 13 vs. 300 ± 17 μIU/mL (p = 0.014). CONCLUSION: In this benchtop perfusion model, islets housed within an ePTFE-based endovascular stent-graft retained glucose-responsive insulin secretion. In vivo evaluation of islet viability, direct immunoisolation, hemodynamic impact, and long-term function is required before clinical translation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Prototypes with a 0.22 μm pore ePTFE membrane were seeded with murine (approximately 5,000-6,000 islet equivalents [IEQ]) or human (approximately 10,000 IEQ) islets. title: Minimally invasive Ayurveda management of recurrent and acute-on-chronic non-healing venous leg ulceration - a Case Report.
abstract: Slow healing and recurrent venous leg ulcers resulting from varicose veins due to lower limb chronic venous insufficiency are common vascular complications. If left untreated, they may lead to severe outcomes such as hemorrhage and, in extreme cases, limb amputation. We report the case of a 61-year-old male with bilateral lower limb varicosities of 10 years' duration, presenting with multiple painful venous leg ulcers that recurred several months after phlebectomy due to patient non-compliance. Physical examination revealed exquisitely tender, exudative, irregular-bordered, multiple shallow ulcers with sloping edges and a putrid odor. The surrounding tissue was oedematous and indurated, predominantly involving the areas in and around the ankle joints. Aerobic wound swab culture showed heavy growth of Klebsiella pneumoniae and Proteus hauseri, with moderate growth of Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes. One month of Ayurvedic intervention employing vrana sodhana and vrana ropana cikitsa resulted in accelerated wound healing in recurrent, acute-on-chronic, non-healing venous leg ulcerations.

title: Beyond stroke: atrial fibrillation and the broader burden of thromboembolic events in the population-based EpiHealth study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the distribution and risk of thromboembolic events (TEs) among adults with and without atrial fibrillation (AF), and to assess oral anticoagulant (OAC) use over time. DESIGN: This population-based longitudinal cohort study included EpiHealth participants recruited between April 2011 and December 2016 and followed through linkage to Swedish health data registers from baseline until the first TE, death, or December 31, 2016. RESULTS: p At baseline, 873 of 22,616 participants (3.9%) had AF and 297 developed incident AF during follow-up. 484 participants experienced at least one TE during 70,587 person-years. Participants with AF had higher TE incidence (68 events, 5.9%; < 0.001), predominantly arterial (73.5%), with 94% of arterial events involving the cerebral circulation. Approximately one quarter of TEs among participants with AF occurred outside the cerebral circulation and comprised both venous and non-cerebral arterial events. Although participants with incident AF represented less than one quarter of participants with AF, they accounted for 40% of TEs in the AF group. OAC use increased from 39.0% to 50.4%, with a shift from predominantly warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants.In time-dependent Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and prior arterial thromboembolism, untreated AF was associated with increased thromboembolic risk compared with no AF (HR 2.53), whereas OAC use was associated with lower risk. CONCLUSIONS: AF was associated with substantially increased thromboembolic risk, predominantly arterial in nature. One in five TEs among participants with AF coincided with newly diagnosed AF, suggesting potential opportunities for earlier AF detection and timely initiation of anticoagulant treatment.

title: Carotid stenosis reporting in Doppler ultrasound: why specifying NASCET or ECST criteria matters-an outpatient study.
abstract: PURPOSE: Carotid artery stenosis represents a major risk factor for ischemic stroke, and Doppler ultrasound is widely used as the first-line imaging modality for its assessment. The degree of stenosis is commonly expressed as a percentage and can be calculated according to different methods, most notably the North American Symptomatic Carotid Endarterectomy Trial (NASCET) and the European Carotid Surgery Trial (ECST) criteria. However, in routine clinical practice, the classification system used to determine the percentage of stenosis is not always specified in the ultrasound report. These methods consider different reference diameters, making values non-comparable and potentially misleading for clinical decisions. METHODS: In this study, we reviewed 1,400 patients evaluated in the Doppler ultrasound outpatient clinic of Internal Medicine at Poma Hospital, Mantova, Italy. All examinations were performed during routine clinical activity over four years by a physician tutor of the Italian Society of Medical and Biological Ultrasonology (SIUMB). The patient population included individuals aged between 18 and 97 years. RESULTS: During follow-up evaluations, it was frequently observed that previous ultrasound reports indicated a percentage of carotid stenosis without specifying whether NASCET or ECST criteria had been used. CONCLUSIONS: Our experience highlights the importance of clearly stating the classification system used for stenosis grading in carotid Doppler reports. Standardized reporting may improve longitudinal comparison of examinations, facilitate clinical decision-making, and enhance communication among healthcare professionals involved in the management of carotid artery disease.

title: The Importance of Family Centered Care and Cascade Screening in Patients with Heritable Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm Disease.
abstract: Heritable thoracic aortic aneurysm diseases (HTAAD) may be either syndromic or non-syndromic. While family screening for all forms of HTAAD has been recommended, providing care to an entire family is often fragmented in our siloed healthcare delivery model. We sought to determine the frequency of cascade family screening in the current era with either cardiovascular imaging (cascade cardiac screening) and/or genetic testing (cascade genetic screening), and to assess the impact of such testing on adverse outcomes in first degree family members. Of the 184 HTAAD patients who presented to our academic center without a known family history of aneurysmal disease, 84 were followed in a cardiology clinic, 40 in a genetics clinic and 60 in a combined cardiovascular genetics clinic for both children and adults. Cascade cardiac or genetic screening of ≥ 1 family member occurred during the course of care in 138 of 184 (75%) families. Complete cascade screening (genetic and/or cardiac) of all at-risk first-degree family members occurred in only 61 (33%) families and varied by clinic type (12%, 10% and 78%, p = 0.001) for those initially evaluated in a cardiology, genetics, or combined cardiovascular genetics clinic. As a result of cascade screening or an aortic event, 461 additional family members were identified as at risk for an aortic event. Of these, 53 family members from 42 families experienced an unexpected HTAAD-related event. Cascade screening was associated with a lower incidence of an event (1/53 vs. 52/53, p < 0.0001) during follow-up. Clinics that offer family-based care and on-site cascade screening facilitate timely diagnosis and intervention thereby reducing mortality from aortic disease.

title: Unilateral adrenal haemorrhage during bridging anticoagulation in primary antiphospholipid syndrome: a case-based review.
abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a major cause of acquired thrombophilia and is frequently associated with recurrent venous thromboembolism requiring long-term anticoagulation. We report a 42-year-old man with primary APS and recurrent pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis who developed acute right upper-quadrant abdominal pain during peri-procedural bridging anticoagulation with enoxaparin. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated acute-to-subacute unilateral right adrenal haemorrhage without evidence of abdominal trauma, malignancy or infection. The patient remained haemodynamically stable and did not develop adrenal insufficiency. This case highlights the complexity of anticoagulation management in high-risk APS patients and emphasises the importance of considering adrenal haemorrhage in APS patients presenting with abdominal pain during anticoagulation modification. A review of previously reported unilateral APS-associated adrenal haemorrhage cases is also presented. Key Points • Unilateral adrenal haemorrhage is a rare manifestation of primary antiphospholipid syndrome. • Bridging anticoagulation may represent a vulnerable period for adrenal haemorrhage in high-risk APS. • Early CT/MRI imaging and assessment of adrenal function are essential. • Conservative management with careful reintroduction of anticoagulation may lead to favourable outcomes.

title: Labetalol-induced hyperkalemia in acute aortic dissection: A rare but clinically relevant adverse effect.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hyperkalemia is a potentially life-threatening electrolyte abnormality often associated with renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) inhibitors, renal dysfunction, or potassium-sparing agents. Non-selective beta-blockers, including labetalol, may also precipitate hyperkalemia through beta-2 (β-2)-adrenergic blockade, although this adverse effect is underrecognized, particularly in patients without underlying renal disease. CASE PRESENTATION: A 59-year-old man with hypertension, diabetes, asthma, and polysubstance use disorder presented with severe chest pain and hypertensive emergency (243/132 mmHg). Imaging revealed aortic dilatation and confirmed acute type B aortic dissection. After initial medical management with intravenous (IV) esmolol and nicardipine, oral labetalol was initiated and escalated to 600 mg for anti-impulse therapy. The patient developed persistent, non-hemolyzed hyperkalemia (5.2 to 5.8 mmol/L) temporally correlating with labetalol dose escalation, despite preserved renal function (serum creatinine 1.4 to 1.8 mg/dL) and absence of RAAS inhibitors or heparin exposure. Conservative management failed, and the patient underwent thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) with thoracic branch endoprosthesis (TBE). Post-operatively, labetalol was discontinued and replaced with carvedilol. Serum potassium (K+) normalized within 48 hours and remained without further K+ lowering agents. Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale assessment yielded a score of 7, indicating a probable adverse drug reaction. CONCLUSIONS: Labetalol may induce clinically significant hyperkalemia independent of renal impairment or typical precipitating medications. This case highlights the importance of monitoring K+ in patients receiving labetalol for acute aortic syndromes and supports carvedilol as a potentially safer non-selective beta-blocker alternative with respect to K+ homeostasis.

title: Association of chronic kidney disease with major cardiovascular outcomes following lower extremity endovascular revascularization.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) amplifies cardiovascular risk, yet its stage-specific influence on perioperative outcomes following endovascular lower extremity revascularization (LER) for peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains poorly characterized. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the ACS NSQIP registry (2013-2022). Adults undergoing endovascular LER for PAD were stratified by preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) via the CKD-EPI 2021 equation: G1 (≥90), G2 (60-89), G3 (30-59), G4 (15-29), and G5 (<15 mL/min/1.73 m2 or dialysis dependent). The primary outcome was 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: myocardial infarction, stroke, or death). Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). RESULTS: Among 22,424 patients (64.6% aged ≥65 years; 36.1% women), comorbidity burden increased progressively with CKD stage. Within 30 days, 556 patients (2.5%) experienced MACE. Event rates rose stepwise: 1.5% (G1), 1.6% (G2), 2.7% (G3), 4.9% (G4), and 6.0% (G5). After adjustment for age, sex, race/ethnicity, ASA class, admission status, presenting symptoms, and preoperative hematocrit, advanced CKD remained independently associated with MACE: OR 2.30 (95% CI 1.50-3.52) for G4 and OR 3.15 (95% CI 2.28-4.35) for G5 versus G1. CONCLUSION: CKD stage provides independent prognostic information in patients undergoing endovascular LER. Advanced CKD independently predicts 30-day MACE with a dose-response relationship across stages. Preoperative eGFR should be incorporated into perioperative risk stratification protocols to guide cardiovascular optimization and surveillance planning.

title: Structures and functions of enzymes involved in primary and secondary metabolite biosynthesis mediated by amino-group carrier protein.
abstract: Thermus thermophilus, an extremely thermophilic bacterium, synthesizes lysine through a novel type of 2-aminoadipate (AAA) pathway. The pathway starts from the synthesis of homocitrate using 2-oxoglutarate and acetyl-CoA. Homocitrate is converted to 2-oxoadipate by sequential reactions similar to the corresponding reactions in the tricarboxylic acid cycle. AAA formed by the transamination of 2-oxoadipate is loaded on amino-group carrier protein (AmCP) via isopeptide bond linkage. AAA is successively converted to lysine on AmCP by several reactions, and lysine is finally released from the carrier protein. A similar AmCP-mediated system is found in lysine and ornithine/arginine biosyntheses of archaea. Furthermore, the AmCP-mediated system is diversified in secondary metabolite biosynthesis with some modifications in various bacteria, including Streptomyces. This review shares the AmCP-mediated biosynthesis system and its contribution to expanding the structural diversity of natural compounds, along with the evolutionary aspects of lysine and arginine biosyntheses.

title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: n n This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp ( = 261) or MHCA ( = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: p p The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. title: Estrogen hormonal therapy is not associated with increased risk of venous thrombosis in total hip arthroplasty or hemiarthroplasty for femoral neck fractures.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of estrogen hormone therapy on venous thrombotic events for femoral neck fractures treated with either total hip arthroplasty (THA) or hemiarthroplasty (HA). DESIGN: Retrospective cohort analysis. SETTING: TriNetX Health Research Network. PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Patients who sustained a femoral neck fracture (OTA/AO 31B) between 2005 and 2025 who were treated with either THA or HA were categorized into groups based on whether they were prescribed systemic estrogen hormone therapy (EHT) within 3 months before or after their fracture. OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: The primary outcomes were deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or pulmonary embolism (PE) within 3 months after their fracture. A matched cohort was created after a 1:1 propensity match for demographics, diabetes, obesity, and tobacco use. Measures of association models were used to determine odds ratios. RESULTS: P P A total of 39,631 patients with femoral neck fractures treated with either a THA or HA were identified. Of these, 330 (0.8%) patients with femoral neck fractures were prescribed estrogen within 3 months before or after their fracture. After a matched cohort comparison, there were no statistically significant differences in rates of PE (odds ratio [OR] = 1.31; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.56-3.03;= 0.525) or for DVT (OR = 1.67; 95% CI, 0.78-3.61;= 0.184). CONCLUSION: Systemic EHT was not associated with a significantly increased risk of DVT or PE after operatively treated femoral neck fractures with THA or HA. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, Prognostic.

title: Functional connectivity recovers canine-human network homology along the evolutionary cortical hierarchy.
abstract: ≈ p = 0.002 p > 0.3 p = 0.93 Mapping functional brain organization between species is a prerequisite for translating connectivity biomarkers from animal models to patients, but connectivity-based correspondence has been demonstrated almost exclusively in primates. We tested whether canine-human network homology can be recovered from functional connectivity alone, using only five network-level anatomical priors, and benchmarked a spectral manifold alignment framework (Laplacian-eigenmap embedding with Procrustes alignment on network centroids) against a simple connectivity-signature matching baseline. Data comprised resting-state fMRI from 15 canines with endovascular permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (pre-occlusion baseline and hyperacute post-occlusion sessions) and two public OpenNeuro datasets: 29 chronic-phase post-stroke aphasia patients scanned before and after rehabilitation (ds003999) and 10 healthy controls (ds000224). Held-out canine-human network homologies were recovered well above chance (top-5 network correspondence up to 54.5% vs. permutation null18%,), and correspondence followed the evolutionary cortical hierarchy: visual and somatomotor homologies were recovered several-fold above chance, default-mode only weakly-extending a gradient previously described in primates to a carnivore. Notably, simple signature matching (54.5%) outperformed manifold alignment (35.5%), indicating that the homology signal is strong enough to be captured without embedding machinery at translational cohort sizes. Within species, canine network metrics showed no treatment-arm differences (all), and chronic-phase patients did not differ from controls in modularity (); a sensitivity analysis bounds these nulls. All results are fully reproducible from shared code and public data.

title: Surgical, endovascular, and systemic management of renal cell carcinoma with intravascular recurrence.
abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) recurrence within the vasculature represents a rare and challenging clinical scenario with limited evidence to guide management. We report a patient with clear cell RCC and level 4 IVC thrombus who underwent successful radical nephrectomy with IVC thrombectomy and subsequently developed disease recurrence in the supradiaphragmatic IVC and pulmonary arteries. Multidisciplinary management included novel endovascular removal of the recurrent IVC tumor followed by pulmonary bilobectomy for progressive tumor emboli. The patient remains without evidence of recurrent disease. This case highlights the complex multidisciplinary decision-making and potential role of minimally invasive endovascular techniques in managing intravascular RCC.

title: A meta-analysis of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt with or without embolization for esophageal and gastric variceal bleeding in decompensated liver cirrhosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate whether transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) combined with embolization could further improve efficacy for patients with decompensated liver cirrhosis complicated with esophageal and gastric variceal bleeding. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Cochrane Library, for all relevant randomized controlled trials and cohort studies up to March 2025. Statistical results were evaluated using risk ratios and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: A total of 14 studies involving 3079 patients were included. The statistical results showed that the rebleeding rate in the TIPS combined with embolization group was lower than that in the TIPS alone group (risk ratios = 0.67; 95% CI = 0.57-0.79; P  < 0.001), and the same result was observed only in the subgroup of patients with gastric variceal bleeding (risk ratios = 0.50; 95% CI = 0.34-0.74; P  < 0.001). There was no significant difference between the groups in patients with isolated esophageal variceal bleeding (risk ratios = 0.83; 95% CI = 0.51-1.35; P  = 0.46). In addition, the incidence of hepatic encephalopathy in the TIPS combined with embolization group was also lower than that in the TIPS alone group (risk ratios = 0.82; 95% CI = 0.73-0.91; P  < 0.001), but there was no significant difference in survival rate (risk ratios = 1.00; 95% CI = 0.97-1.03; P  = 0.94). CONCLUSION: Compared with TIPS alone, the combined treatment showed a trend toward lower rebleeding and hepatic encephalopathy, yet survival appeared similar between the two groups.

Statistical results were evaluated using risk ratios and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

title: A method for expressing two proteins at a tunable ratio allows for studying the kinetics of creatine transport by MCT12.
abstract: M Interactions between physically or functionally coupled proteins are often studied by co-expression from the same or separate plasmids, but protein ratios can vary widely between individual cells. To overcome this limitation, we developed a strategy to generate tunable and constant expression ratios using a single vector encoding two proteins separated by a P2A site followed by short AAA codon repeats that progressively reduce ribosomal readthrough. After validating this approach with the fluorescent proteins eGFP and mCherry, we applied it to characterize the transport cycle of the electroneutral monocarboxylate transporter MCT12, a task that is otherwise difficult to achieve experimentally. By co-expressing MCT12 with the concentrative creatine transporter CRT1 at defined ratios, we were able to determine the substrate turnover rate of MCT12 and its substrate K. This approach enables precise control of protein stoichiometry, facilitating quantitative mechanistic studies of interacting proteins in cells.

title: Combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial approaches for embolization of a traumatic carotid‑cavernous fistula with concomitant middle meningeal arteriovenous fistula.
abstract: Endovascular treatment (EVT) is a useful modality for traumatic carotid‑cavernous fistulas (CCFs); in rare cases, combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial approaches may be applied for embolization of the fistula with concomitant internal carotid artery (ICA) sacrifice and preservation of the ophthalmic artery (OphA). A 62‑year‑old female patient sustained a motor vehicle accident and developed proptosis, chemosis, and congestion in her right eye, while no abnormalities in ocular motility or visual acuity were noted. Computed tomography angiography confirmed the CCF. Under general anesthesia, digital subtraction angiography revealed a right CCF supplied antegradely by the ICA and retrogradely by the posterior communicating artery (PcomA). A left middle meningeal arteriovenous fistula was identified. Access to the basilar artery was established. A microcatheter was retrogradely navigated via the PcomA to reach the proximal ICA across the fistula. Then, another microcatheter was advanced into the cavernous sinus via an antegrade ICA approach. Subsequently, combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial coiling with ICA sacrifice for the CCF was successfully performed. During coiling, the patency of the OphA was monitored through the PcomA microcatheter. Afterwards, the middle meningeal arteriovenous fistula was embolized. At the 1‑month follow‑up, her right eye redness and swelling resolved, and at the 3‑month follow‑up, she had recovered well and returned to her normal status. Therefore, when embolizing the CCF with ICA sacrifice, if the PcomA is well‑developed, the combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial approaches can be used, which may facilitate the obliteration of the CCF and preservation of the OphA.

title: A thoracic SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated tumor: A case report.
abstract: Thoracic SWI/SNF-related BAF chromatin remodeling complex subunit ATPase 4 (SMARCA4)-deficient undifferentiated tumor (SMARCA4-UT) is a newly recognized, high-grade malignant neoplasm that is rare in clinical practice. There is no standardized or clearly defined treatment protocol for SMARCA4-UT in clinical guidelines. The current study reports the case of a 54-year-old male patient who presented with a 2-month history of an intermittent productive cough. Bronchoscopy demonstrated a neoplasm in the anterior segment of the right upper lobe bronchus, which almost obstructed the lumen, with a hypervascular surface, suggestive of a right upper lobe carcinoma. Histopathological examination confirmed a poorly differentiated carcinoma. Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated a SMARCA4 gene mutation in exon 4, classifying the tumor as SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated lung carcinoma. The patient developed superior vena cava syndrome (SVCS), requiring emergent percutaneous stent placement. Treatment also included computed tomography-guided cryoablation and radiofrequency ablation (RFA), alongside targeted molecular therapy with crizotinib. Despite aggressive multimodal therapy, the patient succumbed to tumor thrombosis at 1 month post-treatment. Overall, SMARCA4-UT is rare and diagnostically challenging, lacking standardized treatment guidelines. In clinical practice, cryoablation with argon-helium and RFA may provide palliative benefits by alleviating tumor burden and improving quality of life. Endovascular intervention provides a rapid and effective approach to alleviate tumor-induced SVCS. However, subsequent anticoagulation and antineoplastic therapies require further investigation to determine their efficacy in the management of such cases.

title: Meta-analysis of the histopathological features of surgically removed aortas classified according to the SCVP and AECVP consensus documents.
abstract: The Society for Cardiovascular Pathology (SCVP) and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology (AECVP) published consensus statements on the surgical pathology of the aorta to unify nomenclature and provide a new classification scheme to systematically evaluate the degenerative and inflammatory lesions of the thoracic aorta. The aim of this meta-analysis was to determine the histopathological features of thoracic aneurysmatic aortas, thoracic dissected aortas, and thoracic aortas in patients with a bicuspid aortic valve (BAV). Additionally, the aim was to map how consensus documents and classification schemes is used in practice and research. Articles for analysis were identified while searching for references to the SCVP and AECVP consensus documents, resulting in 174 articles. After applying the exclusion and inclusion criteria, 10 articles were included in the analysis. Four cohorts were analysed: the whole cohort, the aneurysm cohort, the dissection cohort, and the BAV cohort. Medial degeneration was found in all cohorts. The dissection cohort showed more severe medial degeneration than the aneurysm cohort or the BAV cohort. The BAV cohort showed the mildest medial degeneration compared to the other cohorts. More prevalent smooth muscle cell nuclei loss was linked to dissection. The BAV cohort showed milder changes in elastic fibers. Atherosclerosis was comparable among all cohorts. Medial degeneration represents the pathological process of several aortic diseases. All studied components of medial degeneration were present in aneurysms, dissections, and BAV aortas. The consensus documents have been useful tools and assist with the systematic evaluation of resected aortas, although their use in the complexity is limited.

title: Incidence of venous thromboembolism with intraoperative tranexamic acid use in breast surgery patients on estrogen-containing medications: a case series.
abstract: Consideration of perioperative bleeding and venous thromboembolism (VTE) are important thrombotic complications for surgeons. Tranexamic acid (TXA) is an antifibrinolytic agent that is often used perioperatively to control bleeding. Product monographs caution its use in patients using estrogen-containing medications due to theoretical increased risk of VTE. However, no studies have explored this relationship in breast surgery. This retrospective case series aimed to determine the incidence of VTE with intraoperative TXA use in breast surgery patients using estrogen-containing medication at our institution. Demographics, estrogen medications, surgical characteristics and incidence of VTE were recorded and summarized narratively. Between 2018-2025, 188 breast surgeries with intraoperative TXA administration were performed. Twelve patients used to estrogen-contain medications at the time of surgery. Eight patients used an estrogen-containing combined hormonal contraceptive. Four patients used estrogen hormone therapy. TXA was administered intravenously (N = 7) or topical irrigation (N = 5). No patients had incidence of VTE. This is the first study to describe the relationship of TXA and estrogen-containing medications in breast surgery patients. These results provide preliminary clinical data regarding a patient population for which TXA use is cautioned against. Future prospective studies are warranted to better define the risk-benefit profile of TXA in this population.

title: Staphylococcus aureus Small-molecule activators of theClpC/ClpP AAA+ protease.
abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis Staphylococcus aureus in vivo S. aureus bona fide in vitro S. aureus The central AAA+ ClpC/ClpP protease in Gram-positive bacteria is crucial for virulence and stress resistance and has been recognized as drug target. Natural cyclic peptides deregulate the essentialClpC1 and cause cell death. Similarly, overactivated mutants of the non-essentialClpC homolog cause uncontrolled proteolysis and severe toxicity. However, no chemical modulators ofClpC have been described. Here, using a biochemical high-throughput screen, we identify eight distinctsmall molecules that stimulate ClpC ATPase and proteolytic activity. Structural, computational, and mutational analyses define two ligandable regulatory sites within the ClpC N-terminal domain (NTD) as compound targets: a conserved hydrophobic groove and an allosteric pArg1 pocket, both engaged in substrate recognition. These findings establishClpC as chemically targetable and provide mechanistic insight into its regulatory architecture, enabling future development and optimization of chemical probes to deregulate AAA+ protease control.

title: Restoration of frequency-dependent myocardial reserve after TAVI in severe aortic stenosis: an invasive hemodynamic study.
abstract: t t t t P t P P t P t P P t P P P P P max max min max min max max min NEW & NOTEWORTHY Severe aortic stenosis (AS) and chronic pressure overload may impair frequency-dependent myocardial reserve despite preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). We investigated whether acute afterload reduction with transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) restores force-frequency relationships (FFR) and relaxation frequency relationships (RFR). In this prospective study, patients with severe normal-flow, high-gradient AS and preserved LVEF underwent invasive left ventricular pressure recording during incremental atrial pacing at 80 and 100 beats/min before and immediately after TAVI. Systolic reserve was assessed using dP/dand preload-adjusted indices [dP/d/left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP) and left ventricular peak systolic pressure (LVSP)/LVEDP], whereas lusitropic reserve was assessed using dP/d, the relaxation constant τ, and LVEDP. Echocardiography was performed at baseline and 3 mo. Forty-six patients completed the pacing protocol. Before TAVI, pacing produced only a modest increase in dP/d(Δ + 150 mmHg/s;= 0.004), without improvement in dP/d(= 0.329) or τ (= 0.182). Immediately after TAVI, pacing increased dP/d(< 0.001), dP/d/LVEDP (= 0.004), and LVSP/LVEDP (= 0.031), while improving dP/d(Δ + 56 mmHg/s;= 0.050) and τ (= 0.033) and reducing LVEDP (= 0.017). Correlation analyses supported the emergence of physiological FFR and RFR after valve implantation. At 3 mo, echocardiography showed lower pulmonary artery systolic pressure (= 0.002), improved left atrial reservoir strain, and lower diastolic dysfunction grade (= 0.006). Thus, acute afterload relief with TAVI reveals preserved dynamic systolic and lusitropic reserve in severe AS, with subsequent group-level improvement in diastolic function.This study provides direct invasive human evidence that frequency-dependent myocardial reserve is acutely restored after TAVI in severe aortic stenosis. Controlled atrial pacing revealed blunted force-frequency and relaxation-frequency responses before valve replacement, despite preserved ejection fraction, with rapid recovery after afterload relief. These findings show that impaired myocardial reserve in pressure-overload remodeling is functionally reversible and tightly linked to loading conditions.

title: Infective endocarditis after transcatheter aortic valve implantation - data from national registry.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: There is relatively little detailed information about patients with IE after TAVI from nationwide registries. AIM: To evaluate the incidence of IE after TAVI, to analyse the characteristics of patients, infectious agents, type of IE and patients' outcomes. METHODS: A total of 9887 TAVIs were performed at 14 centres in the Czech Republic between 2010 and 2023. Rehospitalization for potential IE (according to ICD-10 diagnosis) were identified. A total of 129 patients were confirmed with IE (27× possible IE, 102× definite IE) with cumulative incidence of 1.3%. The TAVI prosthesis in patients with definite IE was affected in 71 patients (70%), IE on mitral valve was present in 22 patients, 7 patients had device IE and site of infection was not identified in 2 patients. The main infectious agents were Enterococcus faecalis (37 patients, 29%) and Staphylococcus aureus (28 patients, 21%). Streptococcus species were the causative agents of IE in 27 cases (21%). Time from TAVI to occurrence of IE did not differ among the four main microbiological groups. The in-hospital mortality rate of patients with confirmed IE was 27%. CONCLUSION: The cumulative incidence of infective endocarditis after TAVI was 1.3% in the large nationwide registry, with an in-hospital mortality of 27%. Enterococcus species were the most common pathogens without differences in time distribution compared to other causative agents.

title: Single-stage hybrid repair of extensive aortic dissection with traumatic diaphragmatic hernia.
abstract: We report a rare case of a 70-year-old male patient who developed a left diaphragmatic hernia combined with extensive aortic dissection and exhibited signs of lower limb ischemia following a motor vehicle accident. An urgent, single-stage surgical intervention was performed, consisting of endovascular aortic repair first to stabilize circulation, followed by diaphragmatic repair. The patient recovered smoothly postoperatively, with no abnormalities observed at 1-month and 6-month follow-ups. This case highlights the necessity of accurate diagnosis and multidisciplinary team collaboration in emergency thoracoabdominal trauma.

title: Anesthesia and the Periprocedural Management of Large Vessel Occlusion Stroke Treated with Mechanical Thrombectomy: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy is the standard of care for acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion and has markedly improved functional outcomes. While procedural sedation was historically favored instead of general anesthesia due to safety concerns, current evidence does not support superior functional outcomes with procedural sedation compared with protocol-driven general anesthesia. General anesthesia is associated with higher reperfusion rates; however, strict hemodynamic control-particularly avoidance of hypotension-and ventilatory management are critical to preserving cerebral perfusion and improving outcomes. Ongoing trials are expected to clarify optimal anesthetic strategies in both anterior and posterior circulation strokes. In the meantime, the choice between general anesthesia and procedural sedation should consider patient-specific characteristics, procedural complexity, and institutional expertise. Future research should focus on better defining patient selection or stroke subtypes most likely to benefit from general anesthesia or procedural sedation, hemodynamic management, and neuroprotective strategies to maximize reperfusion, minimize complications, and improve recovery.

title: Early-term and midterm outcomes of endovascular completion of high-risk subacute and early chronic residual dissection after type A repair.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Late mortality, progressive aneurysmal degeneration, and major reinterventions remain frequent after repair of type A aortic dissection. This study aimed to evaluate early- and midterm outcomes of endovascular completion in patients with high-risk residual dissection treated during the subacute or early chronic phase. METHODS: This study was a single-center retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained institutional database. All consecutive patients undergoing endovascular completion for high-risk residual aortic dissection after type A dissection repair between January 2017 and September 2025 were included. Completion was performed using thoracic endovascular aortic repair alone or combined with the stented-assisted balloon-induced intimal disruption and relamination technique when distal extension exceeded Ishimaru zone 5. Primary outcomes were 30-day mortality and morbidity, as well as 3- and 5-year survival and reintervention rates. RESULTS: Among 127 patients surviving initial type A repair, 48 (37.8%) underwent endovascular completion (subacute n = 33; early chronic n = 15). No 30-day deaths occurred, and technical success was achieved in all cases. Major adverse events occurred in 6.2%, with no spinal cord ischemia. Five patients (10.4%) required early reintervention. Median clinical follow-up was 54 months. Estimated survival was 97.9% at 3 years and 90.3% at 5 years. Freedom from major reintervention was 93.5% at 3 years and 89.1% at 5 years. False lumen thrombosis was achieved in 89.6% of thoracic and 81.4% of visceral segments. CONCLUSIONS: Endovascular completion of high-risk residual dissection after type A repair is safe and effective, providing excellent midterm survival, low major reintervention rates, and high rates of aortic remodeling.

This study aimed to evaluate early- and midterm outcomes of endovascular completion in patients with high-risk residual dissection treated during the subacute or early chronic phase. METHODS: This study was a single-center retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained institutional database.

title: Estimating Regional Demand for Mechanical Thrombectomy Based on Daily Case Distribution.
abstract: Rapid provision of mechanical thrombectomy for acute large-vessel occlusion is indispensable for favorable outcomes; however, only a minority of eligible patients receive timely treatment. This health services research study examined the daily distribution of mechanical thrombectomy procedures within a regional system to provide a basis for estimating the treatment capacity required to meet demand. We collected daily mechanical thrombectomy case counts in Kochi prefecture, Japan, from January 2016 through December 2023. Assuming that mechanical thrombectomy cases occur independently and at random, we compared observed daily case distributions with a Poisson distribution. After confirming distributional fit, we estimated the daily mechanical thrombectomy capacity required to achieve 95% and 99% coverage of demand. To assess flexibility for emergency neuroendovascular care, we also analyzed daily admission counts for subarachnoid hemorrhage during the same period using identical methods. The mean annual number of mechanical thrombectomy cases was 161, corresponding to an overall rate of 23.2 cases per 100,000 persons per year. Daily mechanical thrombectomy case counts closely followed a Poisson distribution, with a maximum of 4 cases per day. Subarachnoid hemorrhage admissions exhibited a similar Poisson distribution. The estimated required daily mechanical thrombectomy capacity was 2-3 cases for 95% coverage and 3-4 cases for 99% coverage. Analysis of historical daily case counts enables estimation of region-specific mechanical thrombectomy demand and provides a practical framework for regional allocation of mechanical thrombectomy-capable physicians and facilities, although intraday timing data would allow more precise capacity modeling.

This health services research study examined the daily distribution of mechanical thrombectomy procedures within a regional system to provide a basis for estimating the treatment capacity required to meet demand. We collected daily mechanical thrombectomy case counts in Kochi prefecture, Japan, from January 2016 through December 2023.

title: Hybrid approach with thoracic endovascular treatment and abdominal aortic replacement for acute type B aortic dissection complicated by ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm.
abstract: The coexistence of a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm and acute aortic dissection is an unusual and life-threatening condition. We present the case of a patient who underwent simultaneous thoracic endovascular aortic repair and graft replacement for synchronous acute type B aortic dissection and ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm. After deployment of the stent graft at the distal arch, graft replacement was accomplished without hemodynamic deterioration. The true lumen of the infrarenal abdominal aorta expanded, and a secure proximal anastomosis was achieved. A hybrid approach can be considered when different aortic diseases involve the same aortic lesion in an emergent setting.

title: AA amyloidosis in the four historical monogenic autoinflammatory diseases: Clinical burden and insights from a retrospective referral-centre study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: AA amyloidosis (AAA) remains a life-threatening yet largely preventable complication of monogenic autoinflammatory diseases (AIDs). METHODS: We retrospectively described patients with AAA secondary to one of the four historical monogenic AIDs (familial Mediterranean fever [FMF], cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome [CAPS], mevalonate kinase deficiency [MKD] and tumour necrosis factor receptor-associated periodic syndrome [TRAPS]) followed at the French National Referral Centre for Monogenic AIDs and Inflammatory Amyloidosis (2012-2025). RESULTS: Among 181 patients followed for AAA, 50 (28%) had one of the four monogenic AIDs (FMF n = 41, CAPS n = 4, MKD n = 3, TRAPS n = 2), corresponding to an overall prevalence of 5% among all patients with monogenic AIDs. AAA preceded the diagnosis of the underlying AID in 40% of patients, particularly those with non-FMF diseases. Disease burden remained high, with 46% of patients requiring kidney transplantation, whereas mortality reached 26% during follow-up. CONCLUSION: AAA continues to reflect delayed diagnosis, highlighting the need for increased awareness among adult healthcare providers, systematic genetic evaluation of unexplained AAA and early inflammatory control.

title: Effect of fenofibrate on diabetic retinopathy progression: an RCT-Only systematic review and meta-analysis incorporating the LENS trial.
abstract: 2 Diabetic retinopathy (DR) causes preventable vision loss, yet treatments remain reactive. Fenofibrate showed ophthalmic benefits in cardiovascular trials, and LENS (2024) expanded the evidence. Under a pre-registered PRISMA 2020 protocol we searched four databases to June 25, 2026 for randomized trials of fenofibrate reporting an ophthalmic outcome in adults with diabetes, applied RoB 2 and GRADE, and pooled dichotomous outcomes as random-effects risk ratios (RR). Ten studies met inclusion criteria: six completed with extractable results and four ongoing; three completed trials contributed to the primary pooled outcome. All enrolled predominantly type 2 diabetes (one trial 26% type 1, no type-specific estimate). For DR progression, three trials (N = 3,756) gave RR 0.77 (95% CI 0.68-0.88;HKSJ 0.60-0.99; I0%; moderate certainty), 45 fewer events per 1,000; stratification gave 0.80 (0.68-0.93) for the LENS composite and 0.70 (0.55-0.90) for ETDRS step-based definitions (difference P = 0.37). Need for retinal treatment fell under the conventional model (RR 0.68, 0.57-0.82) but at low certainty: 90.2% of the weight came from one pre-anti-VEGF-era trial and the HKSJ interval crossed the null (0.42-1.11), so this outcome is not firm evidence about contemporary treatment need. No trial found benefit for visual acuity or function (low certainty); macular edema evidence was not combinable (very low certainty). Venous thromboembolism was increased (RR 1.52, 1.12-2.06), an estimate derived entirely from FIELD (103/4,755 vs 68/4,767). In adults with diabetes, predominantly type 2, fenofibrate slows structural DR progression but is not established as vision-preserving.

title: Endovascular therapy for mild-to-moderate stroke due to basilar artery occlusion: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular therapy (EVT) is an established treatment for basilar artery occlusion (BAO) with severe deficits, but its benefit in patients with mild-to-moderate symptoms (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] <10) remains unclear due to limited randomized controlled trial (RCT) evidence. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate EVT efficacy and safety in this subgroup. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for RCTs and observational studies published between January 1, 2014, and July 1, 2026, comparing EVT plus best medical treatment (BMT) versus BMT in BAO with NIHSS <10. The primary outcome was 90-day good functional status (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2). Secondary outcomes were favorable (mRS 0-3) and excellent (mRS 0-1) functional status. Safety outcomes included 90-day mortality, any intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and symptomatic ICH. RESULTS: Fifteen studies comprising 3981 patients (1812 EVT; 2169 BMT) were included. No significant differences were observed in good (OR = 1.51; 95% CI 0.89-2.54; p = 0.12) or favorable functional status (OR = 0.99; 95% CI 0.75-1.30; p = 0.92), while EVT increased the odds of excellent status (OR = 2.01; 95% CI 1.33-3.05; p < 0.001). Mortality (OR = 0.94; 95% CI 0.55-1.59), any ICH (OR = 1.23; 95% CI 0.69-2.19) and symptomatic ICH (OR = 0.98; 95% CI 0.61-1.57) were comparable. CONCLUSION: Although no difference emerged for the primary outcome, EVT increased the likelihood of excellent recovery without compromising safety. These findings highlight the need for RCTs targeting this population.

We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate EVT efficacy and safety in this subgroup. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for RCTs and observational studies published between January 1, 2014, and July 1, 2026, comparing EVT plus best medical treatment (BMT) versus BMT in BAO with NIHSS <10.

title: Endovascular retrieval of a fractured Lightning Bolt 7 Catheter from the femoral vein using the ClotTriever Thrombectomy System.
abstract: As large-bore mechanical thrombectomy is increasingly used to treat deep vein thrombosis (DVT), uncommon device-related adverse events, including catheter deformation, fracture, and retained intravascular foreign bodies, may be encountered. This study describes the case of a 60-year-old man with right lower-extremity DVT and pulmonary embolism in whom a Lightning Bolt 7 catheter (Penumbra) fractured during aspiration thrombectomy, resulting in a retained catheter fragment within the femoral vein that was refractory to snare retrieval attempts. During a subsequent procedure, the ClotTriever BOLD Thrombectomy System (Inari Medical), was used to successfully achieve simultaneous extraction of the embedded catheter fragment in its entirety and acute thrombus, restoring inline venous flow. This case highlights a salvage strategy using a large-bore, mechanically distinct thrombectomy device to retrieve a retained catheter fragment while simultaneously treating acute DVT.

title: The role of anti-factor Xa in patients with cancer receiving prophylactic low-molecular-weight heparin: a meta-analysis.
abstract: I I I 2 2 2 Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) is a mainstay in the prevention of cancer-associated thrombosis. However, there is a lack of clear guidelines around routine monitoring of anti-factor Xa (AFXa) levels in patients with cancer receiving LMWH for prophylaxis. This study compares fixed vs laboratory-based dosing of LMWH in patients with cancer to elucidate if there are significant differences in venous thromboembolism (VTE) and bleeding outcomes for this population. To our knowledge, this is the first meta-analysis that evaluates AFXa monitoring, specifically in patients with cancer. A total of 561 articles were screened, and 5 studies were included in the meta-analysis. Two studies directly compared outcomes of fixed dosing vs AFXa-based dosing, and 4 studies evaluated outcomes based on whether AFXa values were subprophylactic, prophylactic, or supraprophylactic. The relative risk (RR) of VTE was higher in fixed dosing vs adjusting for AFXa levels, although this failed to reach statistical significance (RR, 9.27; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.90-95.29;= 0.0%). Surprisingly, patients with subprophylactic AFXa levels experienced bleeding events at 6% (95% CI, 0.00-0.24;= 73.3%) compared to 2% at prophylactic levels (95% CI, 0.00-0.08;= 3.1%), although the difference was not statistically significant. Our findings suggest a lack of benefit in monitoring AFXa in prophylaxis for preventing VTE; however, further investigation into high-risk malignancies or patients undergoing cancer surgery may elucidate differences in VTE and bleeding outcomes that guide future prophylactic anticoagulation.

However, there is a lack of clear guidelines around routine monitoring of anti-factor Xa (AFXa) levels in patients with cancer receiving LMWH for prophylaxis. title: SHR-2004, a Humanized Monoclonal Antibody Targeting Factor XI, for Preventing Venous Thromboembolism After Ovarian Cancer Surgery: A Randomized, Active-Controlled Phase 2 Study.
abstract: This multicenter, randomized, open-label, exploratory Phase 2 trial assessed SHR-2004, an anti-FXI antibody, for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prevention in patients undergoing ovarian cancer surgery-a population at particularly high thrombotic risk conducted at 25 sites in China. Patients with newly diagnosed Stage III-IV or recurrent ovarian cancer scheduled for surgery were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive subcutaneous SHR-2004 (180 mg on Day 1 and 120 mg on Day 15) or enoxaparin-rivaroxaban (subcutaneous enoxaparin 40 mg once daily during hospitalization, followed by oral rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily after discharge until Day 28). The primary efficacy outcome was the composite of VTE events within 28 days. The primary safety outcome was major bleeding (MB) or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (CRNMB) from first dose to 28 days. Between February 19, 2024 and September 17, 2024, 198 patients received assigned treatment (90 with SHR-2004, 108 with enoxaparin-rivaroxaban) and were included in the safety analysis. Among 181 patients who completed protocol-mandated ultrasonography, VTE occurred in 11 (12.6%) patients in the SHR-2004 group and 19 (20.2%) in the enoxaparin-rivaroxaban group (difference -8.4%, 95% CI -19.9 to 3.1) by Day 28. MB/CRNMB rates were similar between groups (SHR-2004: 2/90 [2.2%]; enoxaparin-rivaroxaban: 2/108 [1.9%]). In this study, SHR-2004 showed comparable efficacy to enoxaparin-rivaroxaban for preventing postoperative VTE in patients undergoing ovarian cancer surgery, with a similar low risk of MB or CRNMB. The twice-monthly dosing schedule offers a potential advantage over daily anticoagulation, supporting further investigation in adequately powered Phase 3 trials. title: The Imaging Compass: Navigating Reperfusion in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: The management of acute ischemic stroke has shifted from rigid time-based protocols to imaging-driven, tissue-based reperfusion strategies. Non-contrast CT and CT angiography remain the indispensable frontline for rapid triage, particularly in community and low-resource settings. However, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides unique biological information that complements CT-based assessment: Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) detects cellular ischemia within minutes without contrast; DWI-fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) mismatch serves as a tissue clock for unknown-onset stroke; susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) aids thrombus characterization; and MRI resolves the posterior fossa without beam-hardening artifact. Low-field portable MRI further extends these capabilities to the bedside where conventional scanners are unavailable. This review examines four convergent trends within this transition: expanding thrombectomy to large-core infarction, extending thrombolysis through tissue-based selection, advancing recanalization in posterior-circulation stroke while defining boundaries for medium- and distal-vessel occlusions, and simplifying imaging workflows through fast MRI protocols, quantitative CT biomarkers, and artificial intelligence (AI). Landmark trials have established that treatment benefit is determined by tissue viability rather than clock time, while recent negative trials define critical boundaries beyond which intervention may cause harm. We critically appraise how CT and MRI are integrated hierarchically across these scenarios, and how emerging fast MRI and quantitative biomarkers may reshape future selection paradigms. EVIDENCE LEVEL: 3-4. TECHNICAL EFFICACY: 3.

title: Effects of Sarpogrelate Versus Aspirin on Whole Blood Viscosity in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Peripheral Artery Disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Whole blood viscosity (WBV) is associated with impaired microvascular circulation and cardiovascular risk in patients with Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and peripheral artery disease (PAD). This study investigated the efficacy and safety of sarpogrelate compared with aspirin on WBV in patients with T2DM and PAD. METHODS: -1 This randomised, open-label clinical trial enrolled adults with T2DM and PAD. A total of 66 participants were randomised to aspirin (n = 33) or sarpogrelate (n = 33) for 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was change in diastolic WBV at a shear rate of 1 sfrom baseline to week 24. Secondary endpoints included tissue oxygen delivery index, pain visual analogue scale (VAS) and cold sensation scores. RESULTS: After 24 weeks, diastolic WBV did not decrease significantly in both groups (sarpogrelate group: 31.91 ± 7.83 to 30.76 ± 7.08, mean change, -1.15 ± 9.25; p = 0.509; aspirin group: 33.32 ± 8.86 to 32.12 ± 9.60, mean change, -1.20 ± 8.36; p = 0.432). VAS scores improved significantly in both groups (mean change, -9.09 ± 18.09; p = 0.007 for sarpogrelate; -6.13 ± 16.47; p = 0.047 for aspirin), with no between-group difference. Cold sensation scores improved only in the sarpogrelate group (mean change, -0.21 ± 0.55; p = 0.033 vs. -0.23 ± 0.85; p = 0.147 for aspirin group), with no between-group difference. CONCLUSION: In patients with T2DM and PAD, sarpogrelate did not significantly improve WBV compared with aspirin. VAS scores and cold sensation improved significantly within the sarpogrelate group with no between-group difference.

METHODS: -1 This randomised, open-label clinical trial enrolled adults with T2DM and PAD.

title: Clinically Relevant Outcomes With Romiplostim in Patients With Solid Tumors and Persistent Chemotherapy Induced Thrombocytopenia.
abstract: Thrombopoietin receptor agonists (TPO-RAs), such as romiplostim, are commonly utilized to facilitate timely platelet recovery and administration of chemotherapy in patients with cancer and chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia (CIT). However, there are limited data on the effect of TPO-RAs on clinically important outcomes. A target trial emulation study was implemented to assess the effects of romiplostim in patients with solid tumors and persistent CIT, compared to controls. Patients were exact-matched on chemotherapy, cancer type, degree of thrombocytopenia, and 1:1 propensity-score-matched on clinical/laboratory variables on Day 1 of romiplostim treatment or quasi-index date for controls. Study outcomes included overall survival over 24 months and venous thromboembolism (VTE) at 6 months. This study included 165 romiplostim-treated patients and 165 controls. Baseline characteristics were well-balanced. The median age was 61 years and 52% were female. The median romiplostim duration was 1.38 months. Median overall survival was 13 months (95% CI: 9.9-23) in the romiplostim group and 9.5 months (95% CI: 7.1-14.0) in controls (hazard ratio [HR] 0.86 [95% CI: 0.65-1.13]). There was a numerical improvement in survival with romiplostim (0.80 [95% CI: 0.60-1.06]) which was statistically significant in the subgroup of patients with metastatic disease (HR 0.70 [95% CI: 0.52-0.95]). The 6-month cumulative incidence of VTE was 10.0% (95% CI: 6.3%-16.0%) in the romiplostim group and 8.0% (95% CI: 4.5%-13.0%) in controls (HR 1.31 [95% CI: 0.64-2.70]), with death as a competing risk. In conclusion, these results support the safety of romiplostim in CIT with observed numerical improvement in overall survival at 2 years.

A target trial emulation study was implemented to assess the effects of romiplostim in patients with solid tumors and persistent CIT, compared to controls.

title: Machine learning-derived serum carbon dioxide trajectories in predicting prognosis of patients with acute aortic dissection.
abstract: Venous partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PvCO 2 ) indicates postoperative adverse outcomes in patients with acute aortic dissection, and its trajectories over time affecting postoperative adverse outcomes remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between PvCO 2 trajectories and postoperative adverse outcomes, as well as clinical application through group-based trajectory modeling and machine-learning algorithms. This retrospective cohort study analyzed data from 642 patients with acute aortic dissection treated at the Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University from 2019 to 2024, to determine postoperative adverse outcomes, including 6-month mortality and complications. Three PvCO 2 tests within the first 72 hours of admission were used to analyze PvCO 2 trajectories through group-based trajectory modeling. To diagnose high-risk PvCO 2 trajectories in emergency settings, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was conducted to select key features, which were consequently integrated into predictive models using multiple machine-learning methods. Finally, a web-based interpretable website was developed for predicting PvCO 2 trajectories in patients with acute aortic dissection. Overall, 642 patients were classed into four PvCO 2 trajectories (T1, persistent decrease from a medium to a low level; T2, stable low level; T3, persistent decrease from a high to a low level; T4, stable midlevel), showing distinct patterns. After adjustment for other covariates, postoperative adverse outcomes among these groups showed significant differences, with a higher proportion of postoperative adverse outcomes in the T3 group. Subsequently, upon Shapley additive explanations analysis, 17 features with importance sequence were identified (hemoglobin, direct bilirubin, monocyte, adenosine deaminase, drinking, anion gap, chloride, platelet, lymphocyte, albumin/globulin ratio, calcium, alanine aminotransferase, α-L-fucosidase, D-dimer, antihypertensive drugs, and smoking), which were integrated into the model for predicting T3. The optimal machine-learning model was established for predicting postoperative adverse outcomes. Finally, a web-based interpretable model was developed to predict patients with acute aortic dissection and high risk of postoperative adverse outcomes. This study uncovers heterogeneity in PvCO 2 trajectory, highlighting that decreased PvCO 2 is associated with worse prognosis. A web-based tool for the prediction of acute aortic dissection patients at high risk of postoperative adverse outcomes was constructed to facilitate clinical application.

title: Decoding the urinary metabolome of aromatic amino acid pathways in Alport syndrome.
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) has been associated with alterations in plasma-free aromatic amino acids (AAA)-tryptophan (Trp), phenylalanine (Phe), and tyrosine (Tyr)-and some downstream metabolites. However, AAA metabolism comprises a wider set of compounds, including microbiome-derived and sulfate-conjugated metabolites excreted in urine with potential biological implications. Alport syndrome (AS), a genetic condition defined by progressive renal impairment, frequently advances to CKD, suggesting that disturbances in AAA-related metabolism may also be relevant in this disorder. Nevertheless, a comprehensive quantitative method covering AAA-derived metabolites enabling an assessment of their implications in AS has not been established. Here, we introduce a novel method for the quantification of up to 43 AAA-derived metabolites in urine, including sulfated metabolites. The method is based on liquid chromatography coupled to tandem mass spectrometry and includes six deuterated internal standards to achieve reliable quantitation. A pooled healthy urine sample was characterized, and the method was validated in terms of linearity, matrix effect, accuracy, precision and sensitivity. The method was applied to urine samples from AS patients-with CKD and non-CKD-and controls. Significant alterations across groups in the concentrations of metabolites from Trp, Phe, and Tyr pathways were observed, including 4-OH-phenylacetic acid-O-sulfate. Notably, the urinary kynurenic acid (KYNA)/Trp ratio emerged as a potential indicator of renal function, showing a marked increase in AS patients with CKD, consistent with enhanced kynurenine pathway activation. Overall, this analytical platform represents a valuable tool for clinical research and for advancing the understanding of AAA-related metabolic dysregulation in renal diseases.

title: Periaortic Hypermetabolism on 18 F-FDG PET/CT in a Rapidly Progressive Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: We report an 80-year-old man with a descending thoracic aortic aneurysm and recent pancreaticoduodenectomy for pancreatic adenocarcinoma. 18 F-FDG PET/CT performed for elevated inflammatory markers demonstrated a hypermetabolic hepatic lesion, subsequently diagnosed as a liver abscess, and intense periaortic uptake with new periaortic soft-tissue thickening and aneurysm enlargement compared with prior CT. One month later, CT for chest pain showed further aneurysm enlargement and progressive mural abnormalities, raising suspicion of an infected aneurysm, although inflammatory aneurysm remained a differential diagnosis. This case highlights the potential value of 18 F-FDG PET/CT in detecting metabolically active aneurysmal wall disease associated with rapid aneurysm progression.

title: Durability of a physician-modified endograft constructed using the Terumo Aortic TREO device: A postmortem evaluation.
abstract: Fenestrated endovascular repair using physician-modified endografts has become an important treatment option for complex abdominal aortic aneurysms, although long-term graft durability data remain limited. We present a unique postmortem evaluation of a physician-modified endograft implanted for a juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm as part of an Investigational Device Exemption trial (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT01538056). Postmortem examination demonstrated no evidence of stent fracture, graft migration, or structural failure. The graft remained well incorporated within the aortic neck with preserved fixation and seal. These findings provide the first reported human postmortem evidence supporting the durability of a physician-modified Terumo Aortic TREO endograft.

title: Sex- and Age-specific Outcomes After Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (RAAA) remains a medical catastrophe. Although early outcomes improved, contemporary data integrating early and long-term survival, and postdischarge care needs across sex- and age groups is limited. METHODS: This nationwide cohort included Dutch RAAA repairs between 2014 and 2023. Dutch Surgical Aneurysm Audit data were linked to Statistics Netherlands registries. Outcomes included 90-day mortality, long-term survival, and postdischarge care. RESULTS: Of the 3642 patients, 15.2% were women, who were older (76.3 vs. 74.0 y) and more often required open repair (61.4% vs. 54.0%). Ninety-day mortality increased with age and was higher in women (39.1% vs. 29.1%), but female sex was not independently associated with early mortality after adjustment.Among 90-day survivors, absolute long-term survival was similar, but relative survival was lower in women (5-year relative survival 68.0% vs. 78.3%). Women were less often discharged home (42.4% vs. 56.7%) and more frequently required early homecare (47.7% vs. 34.7%). Reinterventions were more common after EVAR than open repair and occurred less frequently in women. CONCLUSION: In this nationwide linked audit-registry analysis, outcomes after RAAA repair improved substantially, despite lower estimated in-hospital turndown rates than in earlier eras. The higher early mortality in women WAS reflected by differences in age, presentation severity, and repair type - possibly reflecting less favorable aneurysm anatomy. Female sex also associated with an increased long-term excess mortality and greater postdischarge dependency. These findings indicate that optimization of care for women with a RAAA is not confined to perioperative mortality, but extends across the entire care pathway.

title: Key factors for predicting outcomes one year after Meso-Rex bypass surgery and optimizing the surgical plan in children with extrahepatic portal vein obstruction.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To analyze the factors for predicting 1-year outcomes and optimize surgical planning for Meso-Rex bypass (MRB) in children with extrahepatic portal vein obstruction (EHPVO). MATERIALS AND METHODS: From October 2014 to July 2024, children with EHPVO after MRB were retrospectively analyzed. The number of MRB, the type of bypass vessel, and the position of the lower anastomosis were collected. Predictive variables include the diameter of the connection between the left and right portal veins, the Rex vein (RV) diameter, the number of RV branches, the diameter of the thickest RV branch, and the bypass-to-superior mesenteric vein (SMV) angle, which were measured by Contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) one week after MRB. The upper and lower anastomotic stenosis were diagnosed by Ultrasound and CECT one year after MRB. RESULTS: A total of 153 children (median age 72 months, 87 males) were included in this study. Univariate factors include the number of MRBs, the type of bypass vessel, and CECT variables (except the diameter of the thickest RV branch). Numbers of MRB and RV branches were retained in the final model for upper anastomotic stenosis. The combination of MRB > 1 and RV branches ≤ 4 predicts it post-MRB with 75% sensitivity, 86.4% specificity, and an area under the receiver operator characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.832. The bypass-to-SMV angle ≤ 110° predicts lower anastomotic stenosis after MRB with 90% sensitivity, 73.39% specificity, and AUC 0.847. CONCLUSIONS: Associated factors are useful for early postoperative risk stratification. Moreover, the type of bypass vessel and the bypass-to-SMV angle could be used to inform future surgical technique refinement. Clinical RelevanceAssociated factors are useful for early postoperative risk stratification. Moreover, the internal jugular vein as the bridge vessel and the bypass-to-SMV angle > 110° could be used to optimize the surgical plan for a better outcome.

title: Fatal pulmonary thromboembolism associated with excessive nitrous oxide consumption over several weeks.
abstract: A man in his early twenties had been hospitalized due to acute nitrous oxide intoxication, during which a vitamin B12 deficiency and anaemia were also diagnosed. Two weeks later he was found dead in his apartment. Twenty empty nitrous oxide cartridges were found next to the body, and according to his mother, he had been using nitrous oxide excessively for approximately two months. The autopsy revealed a fatal pulmonary embolism secondary to deep vein thrombosis, and toxicological analysis detected nitrous oxide in low concentrations in the blood. Regarding the pulmonary embolism, a coagulation disorder attributable to suspected hyperhomocysteinemia in the setting of vitamin B12 deficiency could be considered a contributory factor - this deficiency, in turn, may possibly be related to excessive nitrous oxide consumption over several weeks. Obesity and nicotine abuse were present as additional risk factors for thromboembolic events. Reapeted excessive nitrous oxide consumption can induce profound metabolic disturbances, including functional vitamin B12 deficiency and associated biochemical derangements. In cases of fatal thromboembolic events in young individuals, this possibility should be taken into account. Toxicological analysis may demonstrate recent nitrous oxide exposure and support the hypothesis, but it cannot establish the underlying biochemical pathology.

title: Shifting burden of major lower-extremity amputations across hospital Medicaid burden and socioeconomic groups, 1993 to 2021.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Recent reports have identified a concerning reversal of previously declining trends in major lower-extremity amputations, driven by a combination of cardiovascular, societal, and hospital system-level factors. Our objective was to determine major lower-extremity amputation risk by patient resources and hospital setting-the former represented by zip code-based income quartile, race, and ethnicity (surrogates for socioeconomic status) and the latter characterized by hospital Medicaid proportion. METHODS: Using the National Inpatient Sample, we identified inpatient admissions with diagnoses codes for atherosclerosis, chronic limb-threatening ischemia, and chronic occlusions between 1993 and 2021. Procedure codes identified below-the-knee amputation (BKA) and above-the-knee amputation (AKA). We calculated sample-weighted, population standardized incidence rates per 100,000 people by hospital Medicaid proportions (defined as quantiles with increasing proportions), zip code-based income quartile, race, and ethnicity. Landmark multivariable logistic regressions-with inflection points at 2010 for BKA and 2012 for AKA-identified adjusted associations between amputation risk, hospital Medicaid proportion quantile, income quartile, race, and ethnicity. RESULTS: In a sample of 2,769,388 admissions, there were 197,018 BKA and 151,018 AKA. Almost 42% of amputations, both AKA and BKA, were reported in the lowest income quartile, whereas 79% of major amputations were performed in the highest Medicaid proportion facilities. Preinflection points for both AKA and BKA, we note a clear, linearly increasing association between increasing hospital Medicaid proportion, low income, Black race, and amputation risk. In more recent periods, elevated risk persisted but became more evenly distributed across hospitals with moderate-to-high Medicaid burden. Notably for income, there was a widening gap in protective effect-adversely affecting those at the lowest quartiles. CONCLUSIONS: As amputation incidence rises, associated hospital and patient characteristics have changed accordingly. Previously concentrated in extreme settings, amputation burden now spans more hospital systems and pronouncedly impacts lower-income groups. These findings strongly encourage re-evaluating the process of care for patients at risk for major amputations.
